item.title: Geoctau questions legal authority behind MRHL leadership decisions
item.description: Former Morobe Resources Holdings Limited (MRHL) Board Chairman Roger Geoctau has questioned the legal authority behind recent leadership decisions affecting the company, including the suspension of its manager and the handling of corporate governance matters. In a press conference, Geoctau responded to media speculations, dated November 14, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Former Morobe Resources Holdings Limited (MRHL) Board Chairman Roger Geoctau has questioned the legal authority behind recent leadership decisions affecting the company, including the suspension of its manager and the handling of corporate governance matters.

In a press conference, Geoctau responded to media speculations, dated November 14, 2026.

Geoctau challenged the circumstances surrounding the suspension of MRHL Manageress (name withheld), arguing that decisions involving the appointment, suspension or termination of a company manager must be made by the Board of Directors.

Citing the Companies Act and the 2023 court case Elizabeth Bradshaw v Roger Geoctau & Ors (OS (JR) 29 of 2023), Geoctau maintained that such authority rests with the company's Board rather than individual shareholders.

"The authority to appoint, suspend or terminate a company manager or chief executive officer rests with the company's Board of Directors," he argued.

Geoctau said the suspension of the former manager was communicated through a letter issued by Councillor Jacob Maragau, raising questions about the legal basis of the decision.

He questioned Maragau's authority to receive company reports and make decisions affecting MRHL, referring to Section 33B of the Organic Law on Provincial Governments and Local-Level Governments (Amendment No. 15 of 2025), arguing that the provision raises questions about the legal status and functions of existing urban local-level government arrangements following the establishment of a City Authority.

He said the Tutumang, as a law-making authority, should respect and uphold laws passed by Parliament.

Geoctau also claimed that the former board was never formally requested through an official letter to present its annual and operational reports to the Morobe Governor or Provincial Administrator.

He said no new board had been formally appointed to replace the former directors, making a proper handover of company records and documents difficult.

According to Geoctau, attempts to arrange a meeting with the Governor through the Chief of Staff were unsuccessful despite the involvement of the Provincial Legal Officer, Provincial Auditor and Deputy Provincial Administrator.

The governance dispute raises important questions about corporate authority, accountability and the legal processes governing MRHL's leadership.

Geoctau said the former board's position should be considered alongside public discussions and media reports concerning the company's management.

NBC is seeking comments from the responsible district officers.

item.title: PM welcomes audit into funds allocated for Papua LNG Development forum
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has welcomed the independent audit into the usage funds allocated for the Papua LNG Development forum. An independent audit is underway into the millions of kina allocated for the Development forum.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has welcomed the independent audit into the usage funds allocated for the Papua LNG Development forum.

An independent audit is underway into the millions of kina allocated for the Development forum.

According to the government, K112 million was approved, with K80 million already spent, however, landowners and service providers claim disagree.

Service providers comprising several hotel owners in Port Moresby have come out publicly, saying they are being owed about K30 million, prompting this investigation.

Commenting on this, Prime Minister James Marape says it is important to carry out checks and balances on monies spent, but maintains that new projects also require new funding.

Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina says the audit is necessary to ensure transparency and accountability in the management of public funds.

Meantime, the Prime Minister has assured the country and investors that the audit will not be compromised.

item.title: Fiscal stability agreement signed
item.description: Herd Base on the Purari River in Gulf Province, the central hub for the Papua LNG early works (Supplied-TotalEnergies) The State and landowners of the Papua LNG Project will get better economic returns from the project.
item.content:encoded:
Herd Base on the Purari River in Gulf Province, the central hub for the Papua LNG early works (Supplied-TotalEnergies)

The State and landowners of the Papua LNG Project will get better economic returns from the project.

This follows the signing of the Fiscal Stability Agreement between the State and developer, Exxon Mobil in Port Moresby, today.

The Fiscal Stability Agreement signed is an amendment to the 2008 PNG LNG and 2029 – 2021 Papua LNG Fiscal Agreement.

This amendment will ensure Final Investment Decision is secured this year, according to Prime Minister James Marape.

Chairman and Managing Director of Exxon Mobil PNG Dinesh Sivasamboo says this agreement is a key milestone that concludes all commercial agreements structured, thus far.

Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina says he is pleased to be part of the signing, that ensures all parties work towards the FID deadline.

item.title: PM announces K50 million for Papua Liquified Natural Gas Tier one
item.description: Given the project size and its economic returns, the Marape – Rosso government stands ready to support its progress (NBC News) An additional K50 million has been approved to settle outstanding commitments for the Papua Liquified Natural Gas Tier one agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Given the project size and its economic returns, the Marape – Rosso government stands ready to support its progress (NBC News)

An additional K50 million has been approved to settle outstanding commitments for the Papua Liquified Natural Gas Tier one agreement.

Prime Minister James Marape, announced this, during the signing of the project’s Fiscal Stability Agreement in Port Moresby today.

The second and third Tier negotiations of the multi – billion-kina Papua LNG have been delayed, as a result of outstanding commitments from the Tier One agreement.

This includes payments for landowners, logistics and service providers.

Following numerous concerns, and the set Final Investment Decision deadline, the government has approved this additional funding of K50 million to ensure continuity of the project.

Prime Minister Marape explained that this funding is separate from the K112 million, initially announced by Finance Minister Thomas Opa, of which K80 millon was spent on Tier One discussions, which took up to six months.

Petroleum Minister Jimmy Maladina was also present at this occasion, and confirmed that the warrant has been released today.

Mr Maladina says Tiers 2 and 3 will proceed, once all outstanding commitments are settled in the coming days, with the Final Investment Decision expected on the 15th of December, this year.

The petroleum minister further says given the project size and its economic returns, the Marape – Rosso government stands ready to support its progress.

item.title: NBC East Sepik receives Starlink internet kit from Wewak DDA
item.description: Wewak MP Stanley Samban handing over the Starlink Mini Kit to NBC East Sepik team (from left) Johnny Kakawi, Emma Kaunuba, DPR Anna Klawe, Wewak MP Stanley Samban, Justice Sangkol, Ruth Maino, and Aida Mainuy (NBC News) NBC East Sepik has received another big support from Wewak District Development Authority (DDA) within 9 months in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Wewak MP Stanley Samban handing over the Starlink Mini Kit to NBC East Sepik team (from left) Johnny Kakawi, Emma Kaunuba, DPR Anna Klawe, Wewak MP Stanley Samban, Justice Sangkol, Ruth Maino, and Aida Mainuy (NBC News)

NBC East Sepik has received another big support from Wewak District Development Authority (DDA) within 9 months in 2026.

Wewak DDA has extended their Starlink Internet Rollout plan to the National Broadcasting Corporation in Wewak with a Starlink Mini Kit.

This portable kit will boost internet connectivity for live broadcasting, reporting, and production of news and programs.

Vice Minister for Defence and Wewak MP Stanley Samban made this delivery today to show his strong support to mainstream media's commitment in keeping the public reliably informed.

Director Provincial Radio Anna Klawe accompanied by staff of NBC East Sepik thanked Wewak DDA Chairman for another essential support to the radio station during his first term of 3 years.

Klawe said, this portable kit will greatly enhance Facebook livestream coverage for NBC East Sepik.

NBC East Sepik now the 7th to benefit from Wewak DDA's Starlink rollout plan, joining Ruprup Island, St. Peter Chanel and Mandi Junior High Schools, Mambe and Banak High Schools, and Ibap Primary School.

Meanwhile, Samban through Wewak DDA has also supported NBC East Sepik with a 100 kVA standby genset in February 19, 2026.

The genset, worth of K120,000 has restored power supply for the radio station.

item.title: WSPHA signs health border cooperation
item.description: A milestone for the West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) was reached on Thursday, 12 November, with the official signing of a Memorandum of Agreement between two major hospitals in Indonesia's Papua Province. Dian Harapan Hospital and Provita Hospital-and the National Department of Health.
item.content:encoded:
A milestone for the West Sepik Provincial Health Authority (WSPHA) was reached on Thursday, 12 November, with the official signing of a Memorandum of Agreement between two major hospitals in Indonesia's Papua Province.

Dian Harapan Hospital and Provita Hospital-and the National Department of Health.

This cross-border cooperation will give patients seeking specialised diagnosis and treatment access to the two hospitals in Jayapura.

The agreement is based on a Cross Border Medical Access Framework established in 2024 by the Governments of Papua New Guinea and Indonesia.

The West Sepik PHA and the two hospitals in Jayapura have now officially signed the papers to start work.

Chief Executive Officer for West Sepik PHA, Stanley Masi, said this MoA will now give the people of West Sepik a greater chance to access good health care services.

"I would also like to mention that this MOU also covers the people living along the border. People from Telefomin, Vanimo-Green, and from the Indonesia side, they must also go to Vanimo, West Sepik and other hospitals in Papua New Guinea to get the service." Stanley Masi, CEO, WSPHA

In 2025, the National Department of Health launched its National Referral Guidelines for Health Services in PNG. This gives PHAs the authority to refer their patients for overseas treatment.

Deputy Secretary for the Department of Health, Dr Dora Lenturut, who was there to witness the occasion, said WSPHA has successfully brought these referral guidelines to fruition.

"For our families in Sandaun Province and the whole of Papua New Guinea, timely access to specialist diagnosis and treatment can be quite difficult at times.

“This signing has made it possible. This partnership offers an opportunity to develop a clear, safe and coordinated cross-border referral pathway." Dr Lenturut said.

Governor for West Sepik, Tony Wouwou, and the Provincial Administrator for the Province, Jacob Areman, gave the province's support for this achievement.

The Deputy Governor for the Papua Province of Indonesia, Aryoko Rumaropen, also gave the province's support to this agreement, urging both governments and provinces to work together to achieve this.

"We understand that communities living along the Indonesia-Papua New Guinea border have long shared social, family and geographical ties.

“However, geographical challenges, limitations in certain healthcare facilities and the need for specialised medical services remain, and that challenge must be addressed together." Deputy Governor Rumaropen said.

Dian Harapan and Provita are both Catholic-run private hospitals. The Bishop of Jayapura Diocese, Yanuarius Teofilus Matopai You, talked more about serving humanity.

"The Church, not only through the hospital itself, but also pushes its people to serve others, to help others, to give care no matter who it is, no matter the race, no matter the religion, no matter what. To be able to bring out humanity, because this is related to human life, which is more important than anything else." Bishop Yanuarius said.

This achievement will enable people from both sides of the border to access proper health services going forward into the future.

item.title: Simbu PHA hosts WHO and UN delegation to strengthen rural healthcare
item.description: WHO, UNFPA and UNICEF delegation pose for a group photo with SiPHA staff and health workers during the joint mission to Simbu (Supplied) To strengthen frontline healthcare delivery across the province, a delegation from the World Health Organization (WHO), the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), and the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) completed a four-day joint mission to Simbu from No
item.content:encoded:
WHO, UNFPA and UNICEF delegation pose for a group photo with SiPHA staff and health workers during the joint mission to Simbu (Supplied)

To strengthen frontline healthcare delivery across the province, a delegation from the World Health Organization (WHO), the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), and the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) completed a four-day joint mission to Simbu from November 9–12, 2026.

Led by Dr. Rajendra Yadav, WHO Representative and Head of Country Office in Papua New Guinea, the delegation visited health facilities across four districts to learn from Simbu's successes and understand the challenges facing rural health workers.

The mission focused on primary healthcare, routine immunization, and essential health services, the backbone of healthcare for rural communities.

Dr. Yadav, in addressing SiPHA's senior executive management and staff, said the delegation had come to collaborate and learn, rather than conduct a formal inspection.

He described the Simbu Provincial Health Authority (SiPHA) as one of the top-performing health authorities in Papua New Guinea, saying he had travelled to the province personally to see what makes its health system stand out.

"We are not here to inspect, but to learn from you. We want to understand your challenges and struggles and how to assist in improving healthcare delivery for our people," Dr. Yadav said.

In a major boost for the province, WHO announced it will donate seven laptops to support the effective surveillance and reporting activities of SiPHA.

Dr. Yadav said WHO will also donate a fleet of vehicles to enhance the work of improving accessibility to health services, particularly for rural and remote communities.

He said the support is expected to strengthen timely disease surveillance, data reporting, and the ability of health teams to reach isolated areas across Simbu's rugged terrain.

Over the four-day tour, the delegation travelled across the province to observe operations and engage directly with frontline health workers, community leaders, and local representatives.

In Chuave district, the team visited Movi sub-health centre, Keveru health centre, and Chuave health centre. In Sinesine-Yongomugl district, they visited Yobakogul community health post, Koge health centre, and Niglguma sub-health centre

The delegation also visited Mingendi District Hospital in Kerowagi District, and the Sir Joseph Nombri Memorial Kundiawa Provincial Hospital in Kundiawa-Gembogl District.

Dr. Kassi Ken, SiPHA Chief Executive Officer, expressed deep gratitude to Dr. Yadav and the WHO, UNFPA, and UNICEF partners for their support and recognition.

Highlighting Simbu's unique profile within PNG, Dr. Ken noted that while the province faces rugged and challenging terrain and lacks extractive resources such as gold, oil, or gas, its true wealth lies in its strategic partnerships and dedicated workforce.

He also extended heartfelt thanks to every SiPHA staff member and their families for their resilience and commitment in delivering consistent health outcomes over the years.

The visit concluded with a renewed commitment from SiPHA, WHO, government agencies, UNFPA and UNICEF partners, and local communities to deepen collaboration and drive sustainable health improvements for the people of Simbu.

item.title: Five-hundred million kina to rebuild PNGDF
item.description: The National Government has committed K500 million to rebuild and modernise the Papua New Guinea Defence Force’s capabilities to safeguard PNG’s sovereignty. Prime Minister James Marape says the funding, is approved under National Executive Council Decision No. 244 of 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The National Government has committed K500 million to rebuild and modernise the Papua New Guinea Defence Force’s capabilities to safeguard PNG’s sovereignty.

Prime Minister James Marape says the funding, is approved under National Executive Council Decision No. 244 of 2026.

James Marape reaffirmed the commitment during the official send-off of PNGDF CASA aircraft P2-502 to Indonesia for major servicing and maintenance.

The 500 million kina approved under National Executive Council Decision or NEC No. 244 of 2026, will also support the recovery of a second CASA aircraft, P2-501, the acquisition of a new upgraded CASA aircraft, and investment in pilot training, aircraft engineering, technical personnel and maintenance systems.

Prime Minister James Marape says this fulfils the government’s commitment made in August 2021 to restore and rebuild the operational capabilities of our Defence Force Air Transport Wing and other elements within the force.

Marape says this ensures that PNGDF has the aircraft, equipment, personnel and technical capabilities required to serve our country effectively.

He stressed that the government would continue to invest in the Force, building its capabilities and ensuring that it is ready to serve and protect our people, resources and our sovereignty.

PNG Defence force commander, Rear Admiral Philip Polewara appreciated the support by government, and called for similar supporting with the Air, Land, Maritime Elements.

Marape says PNGDF is the embodiment of our national sovereignty and deserves the full support of this Government and every government that comes after.
